scenarios.title: No external payment ever lands without a matching recorded approval
scenarios.purpose: Prove the governed write path has produced no completed external payment, and that no completed write exists that lacks a preceding recorded approval (queued intent) with the same approval_id.
scenarios.rationale: U-042 ships dark and the deployed execution kernel is None, so the load-bearing invariant right now is that zero payment effects occur and none could occur without a recorded decision.
scenarios.generating_risk: a payment could reach the adapter/ledger with no recorded approval behind it
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-042 AC: no payment effect occurs without a recorded approval
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only SQL against the live workspace DB; mutates nothing.

scenarios.purpose: Send a governed-write approval tap to /slack/actions without a valid Slack signature and confirm it is refused (401) and produces no queued intent and no completed write.
scenarios.rationale: The only door to an invoice-write effect is the Slack-signed tap; an unsigned tap must be refused before any decision is recorded or any effect occurs.
scenarios.generating_risk: an unauthenticated tap could advance the pipeline or cause a write
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-042 AC: an operator without approval authority is refused

scenarios.title: "Paid exactly once" is enforced by the database, not by hope
scenarios.purpose: Confirm the single-use decision claim and the effect ledger's commit-once/live-hold constraints exist structurally in the live workspace DB, so a replayed approval cannot record a second decision or reserve the same effect twice.
scenarios.rationale: Single payment turns on a unique claim key plus a single-commitment ledger index; if either constraint is absent, a double-tap or retry can double-pay.
scenarios.generating_risk: a duplicate approval could be claimed twice or commit the same effect twice
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-042 AC: an approved invoice is paid exactly once

scenarios.title: Approval and claim state is tenant-first, so another tenant cannot see or claim it
scenarios.purpose: Confirm the decision claim table, the audit/decision event table, and the effect ledger are keyed tenant-first in the live DB, so one tenant's queued invoice-write intent or single-use claim is neither visible nor claimable by another tenant.
scenarios.rationale: Tenant isolation for approvals is a structural property of the keys; a claim keyed on action_id alone would let one tenant's approval consume another's, and a non-tenant-first event key would leak decisions across tenants.
scenarios.generating_risk: a cross-tenant read or claim of another tenant's invoice approval
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-042 AC: an invoice belonging to another tenant is never visible or approvable

scenarios.title: Recorded approval / claim store survives a callback restart

scenarios.requirement_reference: U-042 AC: approval survives a restart

assumptions: The callback service reachable at http://127.0.0.1:8001 is run with --client-config (per scripts/run_teammate.py), so /slack/actions is enabled and requires a valid X-Slack-Signature; an unsigned POST therefore returns 401 with body containing 'invalid Slack signature'.

The callback server's workspace DB is data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 (the approved sqlite3 path), and it has been constructed with the canonical schema (operation_action_claims, security_events, effect_grants present).

In the deployed server the governed-write execution kernel is intentionally None (route BLOCKED pending AC-CKPT-6 adjudication), so the path ships dark and no real external payment is performed; GovernedWrite* events, if any, are refusals rather than verified writes.
GovernedWrite outcome/queue facts are recorded as tenant-scoped rows in security_events with a JSON payload carrying approval_id/state, readable via sqlite3 json_extract.
unresolved_questions: The positive, load-bearing ACs — an authorized approval actually results in the invoice being paid exactly once, and an authorized-vs-unauthorized-operator distinction past authentication — cannot be exercised through this surface without the Slack signing secret and the delivery/HMAC signing secret needed to mint a valid governed approval token; both are off-limits. These ACs remain PENDING and only their negative/structural aspects are verified here.

Because the deployed governed route is BLOCKED (kernel=None → ROUTE_NOT_CONFIGURED) and ships dark, the end-to-end 'approved → paid exactly once' chain (checkpoint → grant → claim → adapter → readback) is unreachable in this environment; verifying it requires the P12 live-writer wiring and a signed tap. Should the founder expect U-042 to demonstrate an actual supervised payment now, that expectation is unmet by the current dark configuration.

The 'approval survives a restart' AC is only partially exercised: with no ability to create a genuine recorded approval (needs a signed tap), the restart scenario proves the durable decision store persists and the service recovers, but not that a specific in-flight approval row survives. A fixture-seeded recorded approval (via an approved seeding command) would be needed to close this fully.

It is unconfirmed whether the driver_probe workflow.sqlite3 already contains any operation_action_claims / GovernedWriteIntentQueued rows; if empty, the count-based oracles pass trivially and attest absence-of-violation rather than presence-of-correct-behavior.
